reason: The cited evidence (E1–E3) discusses oxidation of Ti–Al intermetallics, pure Nb, and a different refractory HEA (NbCrMo₀.₅Ta₀.₅TiZr), but none addresses pre-oxidation of equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr or the formation of a protective scale on this alloy. The key premises about scale composition, barrier function, parameter optimization, and pesting prevention for this specific alloy are unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Pre-oxidation at ~750 °C for 30 min in dry O₂ forms a continuous, adherent scale of HfO₂, Nb₂O₅, TiO₂, ZrO₂ on equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr
This pre-formed scale acts as a diffusion barrier to oxygen during subsequent 800 °C air exposure
The pre-oxidation parameters can be optimized to prevent oxide spallation under mechanical loading
The treatment does not alter the bulk microstructure, preserving room-temperature ductility and high-temperature strength
Pesting in refractory high-entropy alloys can be prevented by a pre-formed oxide scale
